Manchester United announced the acquisition of Uruguayan midfielder Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint-Germain for €50m (£42m), with potential bonuses pushing the deal to €60m. The 23-year-old penned a five-year deal, including an optional sixth year, and becomes Erik ten Hag’s fifth high-profile addition this transfer window. His arrival adds depth to the squad’s central midfield options alongside veteran Casemiro.  

Ugarte expressed his enthusiasm for joining the storied club: “This is a dream come true. The vision shared by the club’s leadership aligned perfectly with my ambitions. Manchester United demands excellence, and I will give my all to compete for silverware and restore the club to its rightful place among Europe’s elite.”  

He added: “The supporters have always fueled this team’s legacy. I’m ready to pour every ounce of effort into representing them and my teammates on the field.”  

Sporting director Dan Ashworth emphasized the strategic fit: “Manuel was a priority target. His tenacity and tactical versatility fit the demands of our long-term goals. He’s a player who thrives under pressure—a vital trait as we rebuild.”  

The move signals United’s continued focus on reinforcing the squad after a challenging season. Ugarte’s defensive prowess and energy in midfield are seen as crucial to complement the team’s attacking talents. With the new campaign looming, Ten Hag now faces the task of integrating his latest signings into a cohesive unit. Any other questions?
